decisions.reason: The C²-in-time/C⁴-in-space comparison class is valid, but the title and Remark incorrectly call every member smooth (C∞). Replaced those labels with the stated finite regularity; the Definition and sampled data remain unchanged.

The cited coordinate and matrix suppliers use zero-based function indices, whereas this definition uses one-based labels without an explicit bridge. Added x_i=x(i−1), e_i=e_(i−1) and matching partial/matrix relabellings. The divergence still sums all three coordinates and is precisely the imported trace; no calculus claim changes.

The determinant expansion used column labels 1,…,n without connecting them to the imported matrix indices 0,…,n−1. F3 and the finite subset expansion now use zero-based indices, including column 0 when n=1. Multilinearity, the trace identification and the O(h²)/o(h) estimate prove exactly the unchanged statement.

F3 requires a one-periodic integrand, but no cited interface established exp(2πik)=1. Added the published Euler identity and proved integer character periodicity from addition, including negative k. Finite convolution expansion, full-period substitution and Fejér uniform convergence then give h=0 with no additional choice premise. Statement unchanged.
